decisions.summary: The nineteen pages are read by quote-check agents in subject batches, their reports kept verbatim under reader-reports/, and the session builds R3 from them; nothing is written to a page in phase 1.
decisions.why: spec FR-001 puts the inventory in the agents' hands and requires the reports kept under reader-reports/; FR-002 makes R3 the inventory. Batching by subject is a working arrangement, not a change of what is delivered.

decisions.summary: Phase 2 is one task per page; a page is done when every sentence its inventory named carries a note or is recorded COVERED / NOT AN ASSERTION.
decisions.why: spec FR-009 requires the pass be worked page by page with one task per page in tasks.md, and SC-006 states the same completion bar.

decisions.summary: Pages are worked cluster-pages first (religion-and-death, vegetation, urban-features, cities/capitals), then the rest by descending inline-marker count from R1.
decisions.why: Neither request.md nor the spec sets an order; an ordering removes nothing from scope. (Dead in fact - the GM's later amendment cut by item across all nineteen pages - but a plan that predates an amendment is not narrowing anything.)

decisions.summary: record-format over every changed page, quote-check over every new footnote, source-applicability over every new key.
decisions.why: This is spec FR-007 verbatim, in the order it states.

decisions.summary: The caravan-inn fix (FR-011) is scheduled last, independent of phases 1-3, so the gate runs once over everything.
decisions.why: spec FR-011 and D4 carry the fix and its GATED route; the plan schedules it without making it conditional on anything, which is what round 1 of the spec review required.

decisions.summary: Part 4 of TO-DOWNLOAD.md is appended as documents are met - continuous, not a phase-5 job - and listed under phase 5 only so the closing report can confirm it happened.
decisions.why: spec FR-005 requires appending to the END of Part 4 as items are found; making it continuous is the faithful reading of the GM's 'as you do that pass, you can add onto the markdown file'.

decisions.summary: No new tests are written for the inn glyph: its lines are executed by the existing lodging tests, removing three removes no branch, and the 100% floor is verified at the gate rather than assumed.
decisions.why: Neither the request nor the spec says how coverage is met; the constitution's floor is enforced by the gate, which SC-008 already requires green. Nothing about the request is narrowed.

decisions.summary: The only engine change is the inn glyph and no live map draws an inn - the six generators that call s.inn() are all frozen legacy (towns ubame, hoshizora, hirameki; provincial cities tango, minami, nagahara) and no live pool map calls it - so the gate is the whole measurement, with no cohort or regeneration baseline beyond it.
decisions.why: Verified independently on this clone rather than taken from the plan: grep -rln '\.inn(' pool/ returns nothing and legacy-hand-authored-pool/ returns exactly those six files (the only other callers in the tree are tests/settlement/test_civic_grounds.py and wip/shiro_daika/trades.py, neither a pool map). This is the corrected text of the edit under review; the conclusion it supports is unchanged and now rests on a true count. A verification arrangement, not a scope decision.

decisions.summary: Defects the reading pass turns up outside the unfootnoted sentences - a wrong number, a stale link, a drifted quotation - are fixed in this work, beyond FR-006's contradictions.
decisions.why: This widens what the feature repairs rather than narrowing it, and it is Principle XIV as it already binds. Nothing the GM asked for is excluded.

decisions.summary: If the real inventory is nearer R1's 864-paragraph bound than its 285-marker floor, pages land as they finish and an unfinished feature is a partial record improvement rather than nothing.
decisions.why: Not a carve-out from the request: spec FR-009 already lands the work in batches and FR-010 requires whatever the pass cannot close to be NAMED rather than absorbed, so an unfinished item leaves the record honest. The GM's own later amendment took this same shape.

decisions.summary: A reader verdict that contradicts the record gets the passage read before the page is changed; agent findings are checked, not applied.
decisions.why: spec FR-003 requires footnotes written from returned quotes and FR-006 requires a contradiction corrected and recorded; checking before changing serves both.
